Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
847 AM PST Sun Nov 22 2026

.SYNOPSIS...21/756 PM.

Dry and cooler weather is expected through late tonight. There 
will be a chance of light rain Sunday and Sunday night. Light rain
is possible again Tuesday night into Wednesday. Thanksgiving will
be dry and warmer.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-TUE)...22/847 AM.

***UPDATE***

Latest satellite and radar indicate showers approaching the
Central Coast with clouds increasing across the entire area. Based
on latest high resolution guidance, forecast is still on track as
this rain spreads south and east across the area through tonight.

Best chances for measurable rainfall today will be across San Luis
Obispo and Santa Barbara counties with likely amounts around 0.25
inches or less. For Ventura and Los Angeles counties, the rain
chances will not begin until this afternoon, but the chances for
measurable rainfall will be less. If any rain does fall across
Ventura and Los Angeles counties, the amounts are expected to be
very light, under 0.10 inches. Given the light nature of the
precipitation, no hydrologic issues are anticipated through
tonight. Highs today will generally be in the mid 50s to upper 60s
for most areas (about 3-6 degrees below seasonal normals).

With the morning update, did bump up POPs for the Central Coast
this morning. Otherwise, no updates look to be required as
forecast has good handle on the immediate short term.  

***From Previous Discussion***

A weak front will move into and through the area today. It will
likely bring some light rain to the Central Coast this afternoon
with a lesser chc of rain for areas south of Pt Conception.
Rainfall amounts will be no more than a quarter inch (and likely
only about a tenth of an inch). Areas south of Pt Conception 
could a tenth, but most areas will be in the trace to .05 range. 
Not much change in temps today and most cst/vly locations will see
higher in the mid to upper 60s with a smattering of 70 degree 
readings in the San Gabriel Vly.

A little pop up ridge will make for a very nice day on Monday.
Look for 574 dam hgts and weak offshore flow. Skies will be mostly
sunny and max temps will bump up a degree or two. Max temps will
come in a couple degrees blo normal.

On Tuesday the ridge will be slowly pushed to the east by a west
coast spanning upper low. The low will remain to the west of Srn
CA through the afternoon and its only effects will be to pump
enough mid and high level clouds over the area to make the skies
partly cloudy (mostly cloudy for the Central Coast in the
afternoon). There will be an increase in the offshore flow from
both the north and east. While not enough to generate any wind
concerns it will be enough to raise temps 2 to 4 degrees just
about everywhere. Max temps will be in the upper 60s to lower 70s
across most of the csts/vlys.

The trof will move closer in the evening and skies will be mostly
cloudy. Rain will likely develop across coastal SLO county with a
40 percent chc of rain reaching western SBA county by dawn.
Rainfall amounts will be under a tenth of an inch except across
the NW tip of SLO county where a quarter inch of rain could fall.

.LONG TERM (WED-SAT)...22/1208 AM.

The trof will quickly move through the state Wednesday morning. So
fast, in fact, that ridging will move into the area in the
afternoon. The portion trof/front that will affect Srn Ca will 
die on vine and will only bring a 20 to 30 percent chc of some 
light rain (less than a tenth of an inch) to the Central Coast 
with under a ten percent chc of rain reaching south of Pt 
Conception. Clearing skies and the onrushing ridge in the 
afternoon will lead to 1 to 3 degrees of warming for most areas.

Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday look rather spectacular. A
strong upper high to the SW will push a ridge into Srn CA and 
raise hgts to 588 dam (~12 dam higher than average). These higher
than normal hgts will combine with 3 to 6 mb of offshore flow and
will bring sunny skies, locally breezy mornings, 3 to 6 degrees of
warming Thanksgiving and an additional 2 to 4 degrees on Friday.
Friday's max temps will be in the mid 70s to lower 80s or about 
10 degrees over normal. Friday's offshore flow will be 4 to 6 mb, 
but with not much upper support there is only a low chance of 
advisory level gusts.

A fast moving trof will knock the ridge down on Saturday. It will
bring a 20-30 percent chc of light rain to mainly the Central 
Coast. Rainfall, if any will be less than a tenth of an inch. More
importantly the offshore flow will turn weakly onshore and this
with an increase in cloud cover will lower max temps by about 5
degrees.

&&

.AVIATION...22/1026Z.

At 0828Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Good confidence in TAFs. VFR TAFs expected at all airfields, 
although there is a 20% chance for LIFR cigs at KPRB from 12Z to 
16Z.

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. Light northeast winds are
possible from 12Z to 16Z. Any east wind component is expected to 
be 7 kt or less thru the fcst period.

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF.

&&

.MARINE...22/222 AM.

High confidence that winds and seas will remain below small craft
advisory (SCA) levels through Tuesday.

Two storms are expected to affect the area. The first will be 
later today and tonight, and another on Wednesday. These systems 
will bring the best chance of rain to the seas north of Pt 
Conception. Post- frontal low-end SCA level NW-W winds will still 
be possible Wednesday/night south of Point Conception. A 
significant westerly swell (around 14-16 feet) is expected mid- 
week, with large, SCA level seas for the outer waters.
